This model extends VG09 (joint understood + spoken with study and subject random intercepts) with a **cross-lag** (issue #113): a child's prior-wave words understood predicts their current production ratio $q$, testing whether *earlier receptive* vocabulary leads *later expressive* vocabulary **within a child**. Because the repeated-measures children are mostly two-wave, the pure within-child (RI-CLPM) baseline is biased by short-T / errors-in-variables mechanics; VG16 therefore **headlines the bias-robust population-relative baseline** and reports the within-child variant as a cautionary contrast. See `notes/202607031200-vg16-within-child-scoping.md`.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
```

## Statistical model

The mean structure follows VG09, with $p_S(a) = p_U(a)\,q(a)$ and study + subject random intercepts on both the understood logit $f_U$ and the production-ratio logit $h$. Words understood use the common 810-word reference inventory; paired, logically nested spoken counts use $S\mid U \sim \operatorname{BetaBinomial}(U,q,\kappa_S)$, with the marginal 810-word fallback reserved for rows without a usable understood count. VG16 adds one **population cross-lag coefficient** $\beta$ to the production-ratio logit:

$$h(a, s, i) = \text{intercept}_q + \text{slope}_q\,a_z + g_q(a) + \delta_q[s] + \delta^{\text{subj}}_q[i] + \beta\,x^{\text{lag}}_i$$

where, for the child's immediately preceding observed wave (age $a_{\text{prev}}$),

$$x^{\text{lag}}_i = \operatorname{logit}\!\big(\text{understood}_{\text{prev}}/N\big) - \big(f_U(a_{\text{prev}}) + \delta_U[s]\big)$$

is the child's prior-wave understood relative to a baseline (0 for first waves / no prior comprehension). Two baselines are fit. The **population-relative** headline subtracts only the population + study comprehension level (as written above). The **within-child** (RI-CLPM) contrast additionally subtracts the child's own understood intercept $\delta^{\text{subj}}_U[i]$. In both, $\beta > 0$ means earlier receptive standing predicts later expressive conversion, and the subject $q$-intercept $\delta^{\text{subj}}_q[i]$ controls for the child's stable production level.

::: {.callout-note title="Model at a glance"}

- **Population:** children with Down syndrome.
- **Foundation:** VG09 (study + subject random intercepts on understood and on $q$).
- **New term:** cross-lag $\beta$ (prior receptive → current $q$).
- **Baseline:** population-relative headline (subtract the population + study comprehension level); a within-child (RI-CLPM) contrast is also fitted (cautionary — see results).
- **Reported curves:** population-level trajectories (all random effects set to zero).

:::

## Cross-lag: earlier receptive → later expressive

The headline cross-lag coefficient $\beta$ (`beta_lag`, population-relative baseline) is the earlier-receptive → later-expressive lead on the logit scale, controlling for the child's stable production level:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-beta-lag
#| echo: false
diagnostics = pd.read_csv("diagnostics.csv", index_col=0)
diagnostics.loc[diagnostics.index.str.contains("beta_lag", case=False)]
```

::: {.callout-important title="Within-child contrast and the short-T bias"}

The pure within-child (RI-CLPM) baseline — which additionally subtracts the child's *own* understood intercept — was fit as a diagnostic. With the two-wave-dominated data it is **strongly and spuriously negative** (dev-tier $\beta \approx -0.60$, 89% interval $[-0.85, -0.35]$): a **short-T (Nickell-type) / errors-in-variables artifact** of regressing on a lag tied to the child's own random intercept, *not* evidence that comprehension suppresses later production. The bias-robust population-relative headline above avoids that circularity and is essentially null at dev-tier ($\beta \approx +0.05$, interval spanning 0). Sharpening the within-child estimate (latent-AR understood; restricting to the ≥3-wave children) is deferred to v2. See the scoping note (§5).

:::
